description: The editor argues, quoting Wainer, that replicability is the principal epistemological tenet of modern science: small initial studies tolerate false positives, and other investigators should rush to replicate so anomalous results are brushed aside.
title: Independent replication of educational intervention studies

description: Baldwin advocates the individualizing method: following the same children consecutively over years with both physical and mental measurements, rather than cross-sectional snapshots.
title: Individual longitudinal growth-curve method for studying mental and physical development

description: Individualized treatment effects, borrowed from the personalized medicine literature, quantify for each student the predicted difference in an outcome between experiencing an intervention and not, even though each student experiences only one modality.
title: Individualized treatment effects (ITE) framework for student success analytics

description: The article develops an epistemological framework based on Brandom's inferentialism for studying students' reasoning on the order relation of integers.
title: Inferentialist epistemology for analyzing students' mathematical reasoning

description: The article introduces \"A pair of information-based methods\" for setting rapid-guessing thresholds.
title: Information-based rapid-guessing threshold methods

description: The report developed a practical means of recording audience reactions in a darkened room using infrared photographs, so that reactions can be related to film content.
title: Infrared time-lapse photography for unobtrusive audience-reaction observation

description: The report applies the ingredients method (Belfield et al., 2018), a methodology that involves \"systematically identifying all the resources necessary for implementing\" a program, pricing each component, and calculating total and per-participant costs.
title: Ingredients method for educational cost analysis

description: A coding system the authors developed to measure explicit instruction and scaffolding of purpose setting at fine grain.
title: Instructional Quality and Implementation Coding system combining Wood's contingent teaching with Meichenbaum and Biemiller's self-direction dimension

description: Instrumental genesis, developed in France by Pierre Rabardel and colleagues, describes how the agent-artifact connection evolves over time through usage and re-design.
title: Instrumental genesis

description: The article uses a two-stage least squares instrumental variable approach to address selection bias in estimating effects of Head Start hours.
title: Instrumental-variable estimation of educational dosage effects under treatment nonadherence

description: The review adapts the technology-based learning framework (originated by Hsu et al., 2012, with six analytical dimensions: learning devices, learning domains, learning strategies, research methods, participants, and research issues) and integrates Pedaste et al.'s (2015) five-phase inquiry framework
title: Integrated analytical framework combining the technology-based learning framework with Pedaste et al.'s five-phase inquiry cycle

description: The article develops a conceptual framework connecting cognitive ownership, mutual evaluation, and selected verification performances so that institutions can make bounded claims about learner capability.
title: Integrated framework linking cognitive ownership, mutual evaluation, and outcome-aligned verification for assessing AI-assisted work

description: The article proposes combining item response modeling with knowledge graph modeling to quantify properties of knowledge points from student self-rated difficulty data.
title: Integrated IRT and knowledge graph modeling framework for quantitatively assessing course knowledge-point difficulty, importance, and necessity

title: Integrated psychometric evaluation framework combining measurement invariance testing and item response theory

title: Integrative review

description: The article identifies adherence to prompts as a major methodological challenge in educational micro-randomized trials, since education often targets the effect of a behavior on a different outcome rather than the behavior itself.
title: Intent-to-treat and instrumental-variable estimation for nonadherence in educational micro-randomized trials

description: The framework holds that learning-related attention follows the structure of course contents, so attention dynamics shared across students reflect course-content-driven processing.
title: Inter-brain attention coupling framework

title: Interaction geography

description: The editorial argues against folk-theory conceptions that label individuals as leader, follower, lurker or lazy, and against simply assigning a leadership role to one student per group.
title: Interactional analysis of emergent distributed leadership in collaborative learning

description: The editorial describes Bridges et al.'s methodological lens, Interactional Ethnography (IE), as \"a logic-of-inquiry that can be used to examine collaborative processes\" as undergraduate students and their facilitator work with multimodal text.
title: Interactional Ethnography and dialogic intervisualizing

title: Interpersonal multilevel analysis of regulation in collaborative learning

description: The IMM is an algorithm that transforms sequences of saccades on the graph area into classifications of horizontal or vertical scanning.
title: Interpretable mathematical model (IMM) algorithm for classifying gaze strategies from saccade properties

description: This report's organizing method is to disaggregate one large survey dataset along intersecting identity axes rather than analyzing LGBTQ students as a single group.
title: Intersectional disaggregation of school-climate survey data
